also: I made up my mind to
I have made up my mind

evidence: Traupman 103: I made up my mind to leave, cōnstituī hinc abīre
terms.comment: With an infinitive, or ut and the subjunctive.

terms.gloss: decide, make up one’s mind; settle (a question)
evidence: Plaut. Ps. 549: rūs ut īrem jam heri mēcum statueram
Cic. Off. 3.70: magnī esse jūdicis statuere … quid quemque cuique praestāre oportēret
terms.comment: Of settling between alternatives, often with an indirect question; with mēcum, of making up one’s own mind.

terms.gloss: decide formally, resolve; of a body, decree
I have decided, I am resolved (to)
terms.grammar: phrase: with an infinitive, or on its own before a future
terms.register: locūtiō plērumque cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; also Cic., Liv.
evidence: Plaut. Bacch. 382: certumst, jam dīcam patrī
Traupman 103: I made up my mind to leave; mihi certum est, I’ve made up my mind, certum est mihi hinc abīre
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: mostly ante-classical, most frequent in Plautus. In this use it means “I am resolved”, not “it is certain” (for that, see sure).

terms.gloss: I have made up my mind
terms.comment: Lewis & Short has the participle dēstinātus, “determined, resolved”; the impersonal use is like certum est mihi.

phrases.english: I’ve made up my mind: I’ll tell his father this minute
Have you made up your mind? — I have.

phrases.latin: Utrumque diplōma pater nōn in pērā Theodōrī, quippe quam puer in silvā relinquere solēret, sed ipse sēcum ferre cōnstituit.
phrases.english: Dad decided to carry both passports himself, not in Theo’s bag, since the boy was apt to leave it in the woods.

phrases.latin: Hominī cōnsilium tunc deest, cum multa invenit.
phrases.english: A man is stuck for a decision when he finds too many options.
